items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own theorem at source lines 1170-1173: the set of infinite binary sequences is not enumerable. The proof at source lines 1175-1222 is Cantor's diagonal argument carried out in full, and it is not a one-step application of a previously stated theorem in the unit. It has to set up the double indexing of an arbitrary enumeration as an infinite array of digits, define the diagonal string by flipping the diagonal entries, and then show by a genuine case analysis that the resulting string agrees with no row of the array: for a fixed row n the two strings differ at coordinate n, and the definition of d(n) makes that difference explicit in each of the two cases. The proof also has to be careful about the direction of the enumeration hypothesis, since it argues against an enumeration of a subset of the binary sequences rather than of the whole set. No result outside the retained text is used.
